Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address City Council, please complete a speaker card and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public
comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote and on matters not listed on the agenda
during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council: Comments are limited to 3 minutes or less and
should be directed to City Council as a whole. Individuals are not permitted to extend, transfer, speak on behalf of others, or yield
their time to other speakers..

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are
available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the
agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has
been posted will also be made available for public inspection. Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City
Clerk’s Department, during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every
other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

Councilmember Valencia wished all a Happy Women’s Month; reported on her
attendance at the Norwalk Girls Fast-Pitch Opening Day Ceremony, Norwalk Lions Club
Women’s Empowerment Tea Party and acknowledged Norma Amescua, School Board
Member, Commissioners Laura Valenzuela and Marcelle Greenidge for organizing the
event and thanked guest speakers Mercedez Quintanilla, Executive Director of Door of
Hope, Stephanie Valenzuela, Teacher of the Year; and Blanca Pacheco, California State
Assemblywoman; reported on her attendance at the Norwalk Little League Opening Day
Ceremony, the Norwalk Pony Opening Day, and Assemblymember Blanca Pacheco’s
Re-Election to the State Assembly event; encouraged all to attend the Artastic Event at
the Cultural Arts Center and the Norwalk Elks Lodge Fundraiser for two Public Safety
Officers who experienced the loss of a family member, both on March 20. Vice Mayor
Rios congratulated all women in celebration of Women’s Month; reported on her
attendance at Linda Sanchez’ Woman’s History Summit, Norwalk Pony Opening Day;
and thanked Public Services for preparing the baseball fields; highlighted that she along
with the City Manager, Deputy City Manager, and staff toured the West Coast Arborist
Facility to discuss the Urban Forest Management plan and increasing the tree canopy in
the City; shared that Social Services hosts a Young Men’s Support Group that meet every
second and fourth Tuesday of each month; announced that the Los Angeles County Care
Community Village will transform vacant buildings at Metropolitan State Hospital into a
mental health treatment and housing village highlighting their Transitional Age Youth
Program. Mayor Perez reported on her attendance at the Norwalk Education Alliance
Annual Mock Interviews, the Norwalk Chamber of Commerce Women’s Leadership
Breakfast, and the Norwalk Little League Opening Day Ceremony.

Background:

On February 24, 2025, the City awarded a contract to Wright Construction Engineering for City
Project No. 7606 – Potter Street Storm Drain Replacement, to replace and realign an existing
section of storm drain pipes and associated catch basins on Potter Street.

On June 20, 2025, Public Services responded to a water main break that occurred during
excavation activities. Based on field observations, it was determined that excavation likely
disturbed the surrounding soil, leading to trench instability and failure, which ultimately caused
the water main rupture. The rupture resulted in significant flooding, impacting an adjacent
resident’s garage and backyard. To mitigate flooding during subsequent rain events, emergency
pumping operations were implemented from November 13 through November 17, 2025. To
prevent further delays and minimize continued impacts to the affected property, Public Services
engaged Mike Bubalo Construction Co. Inc., on an emergency basis to complete the remaining
scope of work, as Wright Construction Engineering was deemed non-responsive to make such
emergency repairs.

From January 20 through January 26, 2026, mobilization and site preparation activities were
completed. Crews delivered equipment, performed saw-cutting of asphalt and concrete at the
Alburtis Avenue connection point, and excavated to expose the existing 24-inch storm drain.
Excavation areas and the adjacent block wall were properly shored. Concurrently, staff
coordinated with the affected resident to clear the backyard, remove existing concrete, and
perform survey work. Trenching operations progressed from catch basin to catch basin,
extending into the backyard as necessary.
 City Council  April 7, 2026

From January 27 through January 30, 2026, pipe installation was completed. Crews installed
12” C900 pipe on properly prepared sand bedding, progressing toward the north catch basin.
Backfilling was performed in controlled, compacted lifts with continuous soil compaction testing.
A temporary connection to the existing 24” storm drain on Alburtis Avenue was established,
representing a key project milestone.

From February 2 through February 13, 2026, final construction activities were completed. Work
included installation of a 10” pipe across Potter Street with slurry backfill, construction of both

restoration. Concrete flatwork and curbing in the backyard were installed, and the street trench
was fully paved. Requested catch basin repairs were also completed. As a precautionary

Background:

  the installation of an athletic netting system. The project cost totaled $18,500.
  4) May 2025 – Field #1 reopened for play. City staff directed Youth Sports organizations
  to be mindful of adjacent homes and only conduct batting practice towards the
  outfield.
  5) November 2025 – Signage was posted at Field #1 to direct players to only aim
  towards the outfield and away from residential homes.

Despite the aforementioned adjustments, neighboring residents continued to raise concerns
about baseballs landing on their properties. Thus, a Request for Qualifications (RFQ) 26-5101-
006 was released on February 26, 2026.

The RFQ requested bids for the installation of poles and a netting system behind the existing
fence along the baseline of home plate and first base, plus the replacement of the bottom 10’ of
chain link fence of the entire backstop on field one at Zimmerman Park.

space uses including an approximately 1.6 acre park. The NTV was approved with a total of
eight planning areas intended to promote orderly and context sensitive growth to create a unique
community connected by a robust network of pedestrian, bike, and vehicular linkages.

Project Area No. 1 in the NTV is zoned Mixed Use Commercial (MU-C) and is located along
Bloomfield Avenue frontage. A variety of commercial uses are envisioned in this planning area
including hospitality uses.

On December 3, 2024, City Council adopted Resolution No. 24-61 approving the Purchase and
Sales Agreement (“PSA”) by and between the State of California and the City for the Subject
Site.

On December 17, 2024, City Council adopted Resolution No. 24-62 declaring the Subject Site
exempt surplus land pursuant to Government Code §§54221(F)(1) and approving a Disposition
and Development Agreement (“DDA”), by and between the City and Lewis Land Developers,
LLC (“Developer”).

Analysis:

Kosmont Partners did a market analysis and concluded that Norwalk, because of its suitable
location in the region including its multimodal connection to major transportation networks and
regional attractions, could benefit from additional branded hotel keys. However, there are unique
challenges in this current economy to locating, financing, constructing, and operating hotels
regardless of the brand or market demand.

To build greater certainty into the contemplated hotel development, the City is considering an
Exclusive Negotiation Agreement (“ENA”) with Hotel2Suites 2 LLC (“H2S2”) to facilitate the
entitlement, construction, and management of a major branded hotel of a minimum of 150 rooms
to be located in Planning Area No. 1 of the NTV.

H2S2 entity created for the potential Norwalk hotel is preeminently qualified to serve as a
complete “turnkey entity” to design, entitle, construct, and operate a full service nationally
branded hotel at this location. The City desires a turnkey hotel project on the site from
experienced business ownership with quality construction, development, and total hotel
operations, management, hotel room sales services, and restaurant/rooftop bar for the Hotel
Facility with an ongoing business plan for the success of the operation. These services should
provide competent and sound design, development, project management, fiscal hotel
management, quality hotel services with an emphasis on maximizing revenues, minimizing
expenses and developing a positive marketing and sales program for the enhancement of the
reputation and image of not only the Hotel Facility.

Exclusive Negotiation Agreements are common tools used with great success to create a
binding commitment between cities and developer interests that typically contain a defined term
